claim: Every code length corresponds to a probability and vice versa, so MDL and Bayes are not rivals at the level of coding. But NML, two-part, Bayes-mixture and prequential codes are different universal distributions, and Bayes is only one choice.
agent_test: Score candidate answers by -log p under the model (sum token log-probs) and compare to a Bayes-style marginal over sampled alternatives at equal tokens.

claim: NML (Shtarkov) is the minimax-regret code. It equals a Bayes marginal only in special cases; for Bernoulli it is within a constant of Bayes-Jeffreys and agrees to leading order ((k/2) log n) for regular models. The two differ at small n and the plain NML normaliser diverges for most unbounded models, so luckiness (prior-like) functions are needed.
agent_test: Not directly testable; a small-n synthetic selection task could compare NML-style and Bayes-Jeffreys choices.

claim: No LLM or agent study found uses NML codes or compares NML with a Bayes mixture. The machine literature uses Bayes, prequential or two-part codes. NML is likely irrelevant in practice for an LLM scaffold.
agent_test: None needed; treat NML as theory. Re-run the gap search with working APIs.

claim: Bayes and two-part MDL classifiers can be inconsistent under misspecification: error stays bounded away from best-in-class at every sample size (max gap about 0.161 at best error 0.2). A randomised consistent alternative exists.
agent_test: Theory only (one proof paper, one group). Not an agent test; informs not trusting a single prior when the hypothesis set is wrong.

claim: Bayes inference with a wrong model can be inconsistent in regression too (posterior moves to ever higher-dimensional models); tempering the likelihood (SafeBayes, learning rate below 1) repairs it in simulation.
agent_test: Same group as K04; simulation only. Test a tempered (down-weighted) evidence weighting when combining samples.

claim: Prequential (online) code length is a far tighter measure of deep model compression than variational or two-part codes: MNIST 4.10 vs 24.1 kbits, CIFAR10 45.3 vs 89.0 kbits; two-part float32 about 32 Mbits.
agent_test: Image classification only. For the agent: score a context by how much it shortens later predictions (online gain), not by size.

claim: Probing with online codelength separates real from control tasks where accuracy fails (accuracy wrong in 8 of 10 settings, MDL always right).
agent_test: Use codelength-style gain (later-token loss with vs without a stored note) to judge whether a memory item helps.

claim: In-context learning loss summed over a sequence is a prequential code length; training on it rewards low error and low complexity together. A big pretrained LLM can still fail to compress a new task (GPT-4 on Mastermind worse than a small trained model).
agent_test: Compare answer sets by the model's own sequence log-loss on the task examples, at equal tokens, vs plain majority vote.

claim: Language models are compressors: Chinchilla 70B reaches 43.4% on ImageNet patches, 16.4% on LibriSpeech, 8.3% raw on enwik9 (2048-byte chunks). Counting parameters (two-part) erases the advantage on 1GB of data.
agent_test: Single source (Deletang et al.), numbers re-verified. The raw vs adjusted split is the point.

claim: Average benchmark score is almost linear in compression of external text across 31 LLMs (Pearson about -0.95 per domain, -0.93 overall, RMSE 3.1%). Correlation across models, not a causal test within one model.
agent_test: Within one model, check whether lower code length of a candidate answer predicts correctness at equal tokens.

claim: Non-vacuous PAC-Bayes / compression bounds exist for large networks, but they stay loose: GPT-2 small document-level Top-1 error bound 96.41%, bits-per-dimension 12.12 vs 15.62 random; MNIST LeNet5 11.55%. Larger GPT-2 models give slightly lower bounds (11.95-12.12 BPD) but not monotonically.
agent_test: Not agent-relevant beyond showing compression-style Occam is only weakly predictive of generalisation.

claim: In-context learning can be explained as implicit Bayesian inference over latent concepts (theory plus synthetic GINC). Bigger models do better at the same pretraining loss (12 vs 16 layers: 81% vs 85%), and example order matters, which exact Bayes would not allow.
agent_test: Check the order-sensitivity of our scaffold: permute the example order and measure answer variance; use order-averaging if it is large.

claim: Real LLMs are not exactly Bayesian: martingale tests show violations, mainly at long horizons (m = 2n), in Gaussian tasks (all but GPT-3.5 violate), and for instruction-tuned models. Epistemic uncertainty shrinks more slowly than Bayes for Llama-2-7B and GPT-3.5.
agent_test: Single paper. Replicate with a current model: feed exchangeable Bernoulli draws in two orders and compare predictive probabilities.

claim: The order violation is small in code-length terms: excess prequential code length is 0.020/0.011 bits (Bernoulli) and 0.039/0.022 bits (4-way categorical) for Qwen2.5 7B/14B; order-averaging over serialisations helps. LLMs are Bayesian in expectation, not in each realisation.
agent_test: Tested only on 2 Qwen sizes and tiny tasks. Test: majority over K shuffles of the context vs one pass at equal tokens.

claim: A Bayesian scaling law (prior over tasks times per-example likelihood) fits ICL curves on synthetic GINC about as well as free laws. The matched-size law (3M+1) interpolates best (0.0268) but extrapolates worse (0.0814) than bounded (0.0621); the larger original law extrapolates best (0.0493). Most real-LLM differences are not significant.
agent_test: Single source, and the extraction in b15/c05 mixed up the table (corrected in critique). Low weight.

claim: Post-training (SFT, DPO) mainly shifts the fitted task prior, not task knowledge, so many-shot jailbreaking still saturates the posterior in Llama 3.1 8B.
agent_test: Single source, interpretation model-dependent. Test: does a long run of confident wrong exemplars override a stated prior at equal tokens.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs plateau after round 1 in a 5-round Bayesian preference task; fine-tuning on the Bayesian Assistant's own guesses beats fine-tuning on oracle answers and gives about 80% agreement with the Bayesian Assistant, with transfer to hotels and web shopping. Caveat: Gemma original reaches about 60% when human preferences match its prior.
agent_test: Needs training, so out of scope; but a scaffold could keep and update an explicit posterior table over hypotheses and compare with plain chat at equal tokens.

claim: Transformers trained on prior-sampled tasks (PFNs) approximate Bayesian posteriors in one pass (near-perfect GP mimicry, over 200-fold speedups), and meta-training on universal-machine data moves LSTMs/Transformers toward Solomonoff induction (regret near CTW on variable-order Markov sources).
agent_test: Both need training. Not scaffold-testable.

claim: Ideal MDL equals Bayes with the algorithmic universal prior (2^-K), valid under the Fundamental Inequality; it is incomputable and reference-machine dependent.
agent_test: Not testable; use only as a bridge: a shorter hypothesis gets more prior weight.

claim: The Bayesian marginal likelihood (code length of a Bayes mixture) can be negatively correlated with generalisation and cause under- and over-fitting in hyperparameter learning; the conditional marginal likelihood (score later points) stays positive.
agent_test: Single group. Test: choose between candidates by held-back conditional score (how well the candidate predicts later examples) vs total score.

claim: Choosing a prompt by mutual information with no labels gets on average 90% of the way from average to best template.
agent_test: Replicate on current models; cheap at equal tokens if output probabilities are available.

claim: Giving LLM scientist agents domain context (a prior) did not reliably help, and letting them write a PyMC model did not consistently beat plain GPT-4o; they chose overly simple forms. Larger and instruction-tuned models beat reasoning-tuned OpenThinker.
agent_test: One benchmark (BoxingGym). Check that explicit-prior prompts help or hurt on our tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Lasso and similar penalties are MDL estimators with luckiness functions (not normalised priors); sparsity prefers few nonzero parameters.
agent_test: Theory only.

claim: Selecting by code length (summed log-probability) alone loses to majority vote, but a joint reasoning-plus-answer log-probability score (PiCSAR) beat self-consistency in 37 of 40 comparisons, often at fewer samples. Self-certainty and perplexity trail voting on math.
agent_test: Run argmax joint log-prob, vote, and vote weighted by log-prob on our tasks at equal samples; add a prior term as a fourth arm.

claim: For reasoning models, shorter finished chains for the same question are more often correct (shortest vs longest up to +34.5 points; shortest beats random), and very long thinking lowers accuracy. Description length of a chain is a usable correctness signal, but only for reasoning models and within a question.
agent_test: Prefer the shortest finished chain, then vote (short-m@k); drop failed branches before continuing.

claim: Two-part MDL objectives have been used inside LLM pipelines: rule consolidation for tool agents (RIMRULE, +4.5 to +4.6 points over prompt-based consolidation) and sample-graph aggregation (MIDGARD, above greedy decoding).
agent_test: Prune the scaffold's rule store with a length-plus-uncorrected-failures score and compare with an LLM summary.

claim: Marginal-likelihood weighting over LLM-written candidate programs collapses onto one model under misspecification (weight 0.998 to 1.000 on 3 tasks); stacking by held-out predictive score spreads the weight with the same held-out score. A safe-Bayes style remedy exists but tempering itself is untested.
agent_test: Do not weight candidate hypotheses by raw marginal likelihood; use held-out fit or a tempered score.

claim: Order violations of the martingale property and shuffle-averaging gains are measured only for 7-9B models (log-loss gain 0.098 to 0.104 nats/token; dispersion grows like log n); no study of frontier reasoning models or of an accuracy gain at equal tokens.
agent_test: Leave open. If tested, shuffle evidence order m=2 to 4 times and compare against m-times samples.

claim: No LLM or agent work using NML, luckiness functions or minimax-regret selection was found (weak negative: search tools were rate limited). Only two-part MDL and Bayes mixtures are used in practice.
agent_test: NML remains theory-only for the agent.

claim: Agent memory systems mostly score below plain chunked RAG (e.g. LongMemEval-s RAG 72.2 / 81.4 / 90.0, all memory systems lower); no study tests prequential gain as the note-value score.
agent_test: Keep raw source recoverable; test loss-change scoring only against a RAG baseline.
